verses.note: The story of humanity outside the garden begins here. Genesis will keep moving people east, away from God's presence (4:16, 11:2), and Israel's own later exile from its land repeats this first banishment.

Cain goes out "from the presence of the LORD", further east than his parents. Genesis keeps tracking eastward movement away from God (11:2), and the reversal of that exile is one of Scripture's great hopes.
The family is saved by going down into a foreign land. The pattern of a remnant preserved outside the land, and brought through it, returns in Israel's later history in Babylon.
